Render a linked Mosaic + deck.gl visualization

Source: R/mosaic_gl.R
mosaic_gl.Rd

Bundles vgplot and deck.gl into one browser scope, with a shared DuckDB-WASM coordinator and `vg.Selection.crossfilter()` so that any panel that brushes/toggles/lassoes contributes a clause that filters every other panel.

Usage

mosaic_gl(
  spec,
  con = NULL,
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  element_id = NULL,
  data_transport = c("auto", "inline", "file"),
  data_dir = NULL
)

Arguments

spec

A spec built with [mgl_spec()] (or a plain list with the same structure).

con

Optional DBI connection to an R-side DuckDB used to hydrate `mgl_data(type = "duckdb")` references. Pass an existing connection so spatial / nanoarrow / geoarrow extensions you've already configured are reused. The connection is never disconnected by this package, in a Shiny session or otherwise: the caller owns its lifetime.

width, height

Widget dimensions.

element_id

Optional DOM id.

data_transport

How query-backed sources (`mgl_data(type = "duckdb")`) reach the browser. `"inline"` embeds each result set as base64 in the widget JSON; `"file"` streams it into `data_dir` and the page fetches the file by relative URL, so nothing is copied into the HTML; `"auto"` (the default) picks `"file"` when `data_dir` is given and `"inline"` otherwise. Both transports let DuckDB write the file itself (COPY ... FORMAT ARROWS when the community 'nanoarrow' extension loads, else a record-batch stream through `arrow::write_ipc_stream()`, else COPY ... FORMAT PARQUET), so the rows are never materialised in R. Each envelope records the rung used in `exportMethod`; `options(dbVisuals.export_methods = "copy_parquet")` (or any subset of `"copy_arrows"`, `"record_batch_stream"`, `"copy_parquet"`) restricts the ladder, mainly for diagnostics. `type = "table"` data frames are always embedded inline because they already live in R.

data_dir

Directory that receives the exported files under `data_transport = "file"`; when omitted a session temporary directory is used. The files travel with the widget as an html dependency attachment, so the RStudio Viewer, Shiny and `htmlwidgets::saveWidget(selfcontained = FALSE)` all resolve them (`selfcontained = TRUE` is not supported for file transport).

Value

An htmlwidget.

Internet access

The widget loads 'DuckDB-WASM' from a public content delivery network (jsDelivr) when it is displayed, so viewing it requires internet access.

Security

In a Shiny session with `con` supplied, the widget's query channel runs the SQL that the page sends on `con`. That is harmless when the app is used locally, but in an app deployed to other users any visitor can send SQL to that connection, and 'DuckDB' SQL can read files the server process can read. For a deployed app, pass a read-only connection and disable external access first, e.g. `DBI::dbExecute(con, "SET enable_external_access = false")` followed by `DBI::dbExecute(con, "SET lock_configuration = true")`.

Examples

cells <- data.frame(cell_ID = sprintf("c%02d", 1:50),
                    x = stats::runif(50), y = stats::runif(50),
                    total_expr = stats::rpois(50, 20))
spec <- mgl_spec(
  data   = list(cells = mgl_data(type = "table", df = cells)),
  params = list(sel = list(select = "crossfilter")),
  vconcat = list(
    list(plot = list(
      list(mark = "rectY", data = list(from = "cells", filterBy = "$sel"),
           x = list(bin = "total_expr"), y = list(count = NULL)),
      list(select = "intervalX", as = "$sel")),
      width = 400, height = 120),
    mgl_deckgl(
      id = "map", filter_by = "$sel", width = 400, height = 300,
      layers = list(list(`@@type` = "ScatterplotLayer", id = "cells",
                         data = "cells", getPosition = "@@=[x, y]",
                         getRadius = 3, radiusUnits = "pixels")))
  )
)
# Building the widget serialises the data frame with 'arrow'.
if (requireNamespace("arrow", quietly = TRUE)) {
  widget <- mosaic_gl(spec)
  if (interactive()) widget
}
